name: TSLint
covers: The 74 TSLint core rules ported to Rerail that pass TSLint's own test suite, with TSLint's default options.

rules.title: Enforces function overloads to be consecutive
Arrow bodies whose only statement is `return <expr>` should use the expression form
Disallows the comma operator, except as a for-loop incrementor
Bans `// @ts-ignore` comments
An interface or type literal with only a call signature should be a function type
Enforces PascalCased class and interface names
Cyclomatic complexity threshold 20
Prevents using the built-in Function constructor (Function or new Function)
Bans ++ and --
Interface names must start with a capitalized I
Prefer an interface over a type alias of an object type literal
Disallows void outside of return types and generic type arguments
Only allows labels on do/for/while/switch statements
Enforces LF line endings
Requires explicit visibility on class methods and properties
Requires parentheses when invoking a constructor via the new keyword
Disallows <T>x type assertions
Disallows usages of `any` as a type declaration
Disallows use of arguments.callee
Flags async functions whose block body has no await or return, searching the body to any depth
Disallows bitwise operators
Disallows assignments in if/while/do/for conditions and ternary conditions
Bans all console methods
Disallows access to the constructors of String, Number, and Boolean
Disallows debugger statements
Disallows default exports in ES6-style modules
Disallows multiple imports from the same module
Prevents duplicate cases in switch statements
Forbids empty interfaces
Disallows empty blocks
Disallows eval function invocations
Disallows iterating over an object with a for-in loop
Avoid import statements with side-effect
Disallows explicit number/boolean/string annotations on variables, parameters and properties initialized to a literal of that type
Disallows internal `module`
Disallows using the `this` keyword outside of classes
Disallows irregular whitespace within a file, including strings and comments
Disallows magic numbers outside declarations/initializers
Disallows mergeable namespaces in the same file
Warns on `constructor` signatures in interfaces/type literals, on `new
Disallows top-level `namespace`/`module` declarations
Disallows non-null assertions using the `!` postfix operator
Disallows the null keyword outside type positions
Disallows parameter properties in class constructors
Disallows invocation of require
Disallows unnecessary `return await`, including awaits in arrow expression bodies and in tail positions of parens, ||, &&, comma and ?
Flags throwing plain strings
Disallows importing any submodule of a non-relative package

caught.text:
import map from "lodash/map";

export const double = (values: number[]): number[] => map(values, value => value * 2);

passes.text:
import { map } from "lodash";

export const double = (values: number[]): number[] => map(values, value => value * 2);

rules.title: Flags a case/default clause reached by fall-through from a non-empty previous clause that does not end control flow and has no trailing `falls through` comment
Flags relational/equality/logical comparisons whose two sides are the same literal, identifier or property access
Disallows assigning `this` into a local variable
Flags non-extending class declarations that are empty, constructor-only, or static-only, at the `class` keyword
Forbids initializing variables, binding elements, and function/method parameters to `undefined`
Disallows return, throw, break and continue that escape a finally block
Disallows expression statements whose value is discarded unless they are calls, assignments, increments, delete, await or yield
Disallows usage of the var keyword
Checks that decimal literals begin with '0.' not just '.', have no trailing zeros, no leading zeros, and uppercase hex
Disallows multiple variable definitions in the same declaration statement, including for-loop initializers
Disallows traditional function expressions and declarations
Flags an if/else whose two branches, through single-statement blocks, are each one `$X = <one-line value>` to the same $X
Flags class methods with a body, not static, that never use `this` or `super` outside nested functions, object/class methods and nested classes
Prefer `foo(): void` over `foo: () => void` in interfaces and types
Flags an if/else-if chain with an else, whose conditions are `||` trees of `$X === <simple>` with one simple $X, comparing at least 3 values in total
Prefer template literals over string concatenation
Enforces double-quoted string literals
Requires the radix parameter for parseInt
Disallows `this` whose nearest enclosing class member is static
Requires a default case in all switch statements
Requires === and !== in place of == and !=
Type literal members must be separated by ';'
Ensures typeof expressions are only compared to valid typeof result literals
Flags the `else` of an if whose then-branch is, or ends with, a return/throw/break/continue, unless an if up the direct else-if chain does not end with one
Enforces use of isNaN instead of comparing to NaN
Checks variable/parameter/property names for lowerCamelCase or UPPER_CASE
